choices.result: They send a much longer theory involving flags. You prove nothing and sleep badly.
choices.journal: I wasted an evening arguing about bogus legal advice.

rows.reason: Courtroom posing never claims to alter evidence or the judgment.

before.title: Your good side is not a defence
before.body: With your {offence} hearing in {caseCity} approaching, you catch yourself practising a dignified courtroom expression in a reflection. It looks alarmingly like constipation.

choices.label: Stop posing and review the hearing details
choices.title: Preparation has fewer cheekbones
choices.result: You check the practical information. At least you now know what you need to remember besides your best angle.
choices.journal: I reviewed practical details instead of rehearsing a courtroom pose.

choices.label: Try the expression once more and laugh
choices.title: The serious face needs work
choices.result: The second attempt is worse. Laughing at it releases some tension without changing what is ahead.
choices.journal: I laughed at my attempt to look dignified before a hearing.

choices.label: Perfect a look of misunderstood innocence
choices.title: A difficult role
choices.result: After twenty minutes, you look guilty of something entirely new. Fortunately, the reflection is not a witness.
choices.journal: I spent too long rehearsing how I wanted to look in court.

rows.reason: Cupboard Professor nickname offers friendly play, refusal and a hurtful insult.

before.title: The Professor has concerns
before.body: At {facility}, {prisonPeer} starts calling you “Professor” after you correctly explain how a cupboard door opens. You sense an opportunity to acquire completely undeserved prestige.

choices.label: Accept the title and thank your imaginary faculty
choices.title: A very small university
choices.result: {prisonPeer} laughs. You agree your expertise ends at cupboards, which keeps the joke friendly.
choices.journal: I shared a joke with {prisonPeer} about an undeserved nickname.

choices.label: Ask them to use your actual name
choices.title: No honorary degree required
choices.result: {prisonPeer} drops it. You lose a joke you did not enjoy and gain a little less attention.
choices.journal: I asked {prisonPeer} not to use a prison nickname.

choices.label: Give them a much nastier nickname
choices.title: A joke changes owners
choices.result: You laugh first. {prisonPeer} does not join in, and the conversation finishes without a graduation ceremony.
choices.journal: I upset {prisonPeer} by answering a nickname with an insult.

rows.reason: Helicopter cartoon is confined to paper and creates no escape attempt.

before.title: The mastermind needs an eraser
before.body: {prisonPeer} shows you a puzzle maze at {facility} and says they are excellent at escaping anything. Their pencil line runs directly through three printed walls.

choices.label: Solve it together without crossing the walls
choices.title: An escape confined to paper
choices.result: You find the actual route. {prisonPeer} insists the walls were printed unusually close together.
choices.journal: I solved a paper maze with {prisonPeer}.

choices.label: Draw a helicopter over the finish line
choices.title: An extremely generous puzzle budget
choices.result: {prisonPeer} adds a parachute. The escape becomes a cartoon, which is considerably more enjoyable.
choices.journal: I turned a difficult paper maze into a joke with {prisonPeer}.

choices.label: Explain why their mastermind career is doomed
choices.title: Walls remain between you
choices.result: {prisonPeer} folds the page before you finish. You have solved the problem of being asked again.
choices.journal: I mocked {prisonPeer} over a failed paper puzzle.

rows.reason: Give the serious boundary a practical response while preserving the comic alternatives.

before.title: Inner peace sounds terrible
before.body: At {facility}, {prisonPeer} boasts that their snoring proves they sleep with a clear conscience. You have heard industrial machinery with a lighter conscience.

choices.label: Ask them to take the noise seriously
choices.title: An awkward conversation stays civil
choices.result: {prisonPeer} is embarrassed, but listens. There is no instant cure; at least they stop calling it a gift.
choices.journal: I spoke honestly with {prisonPeer} about their snoring.

choices.label: Ask whether the conscience needs an oil change
choices.title: The engine laughs
choices.result: {prisonPeer} laughs so hard they briefly reproduce the noise. You wish the demonstration had been less accurate.
choices.journal: I shared a joke about snoring with {prisonPeer}.

choices.label: Perform an unkindly accurate impression
choices.title: A short and unpopular concert
choices.result: {prisonPeer} tells you to stop. You enjoy your own performance enough to make the conversation worse.
choices.journal: I offended {prisonPeer} by mocking their snoring.

after.title: Inner peace sounds terrible
after.body: At {facility}, {prisonPeer} boasts that their snoring proves they sleep with a clear conscience. You have heard industrial machinery with a lighter conscience.

choices.label: Ask them to take the noise seriously
choices.title: An awkward conversation stays civil
choices.result: You ask {prisonPeer} to stop treating your lost sleep as a compliment. They look embarrassed and agree to take the complaint seriously. Nobody promises a silent night.
choices.journal: I spoke honestly with {prisonPeer} about their snoring.

choices.label: Ask whether the conscience needs an oil change
choices.title: The engine laughs
choices.result: {prisonPeer} starts laughing at the oil-change suggestion and makes almost exactly the same noise. You point. They laugh harder, proving your case much too well.
choices.journal: I shared a joke about snoring with {prisonPeer}.

choices.label: Perform an unkindly accurate impression
choices.title: A short and unpopular concert
choices.result: You deliver the whole performance, including a final choking snort. {prisonPeer} asks you to stop. You repeat the best bit and receive no applause.
choices.journal: I offended {prisonPeer} by mocking their snoring.

rows.reason: Serious unfamiliar freedom needs no extra joke or forced major consequence.

before.title: You can just leave
before.body: Since leaving {facility}, you sometimes catch yourself waiting for permission to do ordinary things. Today you stand at the exit of a public building, then remember the door is available to you.

choices.label: Step outside and choose where to go
choices.title: A small choice is still yours
choices.result: You head out when you want to. The moment matters more than the distance you walk.
choices.journal: I noticed a small freedom while adjusting to life after custody.

choices.label: Give yourself a moment before moving
choices.title: There is no bell
choices.result: You take a breath. Getting used to freedom is allowed to take longer than opening a door.
choices.journal: I gave myself time while adjusting to life after release.

choices.label: Tell yourself you should be over this
choices.title: An old timetable gets a new voice
choices.result: You leave, but spend the walk arguing with yourself. The criticism feels unpleasantly familiar.
choices.journal: I criticised myself for taking time to adjust after custody.

rows.reason: Keep memories factual in scope and give the child a distinct reaction to each answer.

before.title: A question about your own life
before.body: {child} asks what you were like at their age. You realise your usual answer is mostly a list of things they should be doing differently.

choices.label: Describe an ordinary uncertainty you had
choices.title: A person before a parent
choices.result: {child} asks another question. An honest uncertainty gives them more to recognise than a polished example.
choices.journal: I told {child} about an uncertainty from my own younger life.

choices.label: Share a harmless embarrassing memory
choices.title: The family gains another story
choices.result: You both laugh. Being the older person does not require having been sensible at every earlier age.
choices.journal: I shared an embarrassing younger memory with {child}.

choices.label: Turn the answer into another lesson
choices.title: The question changes shape
choices.result: {child} listens politely and asks no follow-up. They wanted to know you, not receive another assignment.
choices.journal: I turned {child}’s question about my life into advice.

after.title: A question about your own life
after.body: {child} asks what you were like at their age. You realise your usual answer is mostly a list of things they should be doing differently.

choices.label: Describe an ordinary uncertainty you had
choices.title: A person before a parent
choices.result: You describe not knowing what came next. {child} asks why you never mentioned that part before. You admit it made a poor introduction to your usual advice.
choices.journal: I told {child} about an uncertainty from my own younger life.

choices.label: Share a harmless embarrassing memory
choices.title: The family gains another story
choices.result: You tell a harmless story in which you were very sure and very wrong. {child} asks you to repeat the part where you were sure. They are enjoying that detail.
choices.journal: I shared an embarrassing younger memory with {child}.

choices.label: Turn the answer into another lesson
choices.title: The question changes shape
choices.result: You begin “What you need to understand”. {child} nods, puts away their question and lets you finish. You never get around to saying what you were like.
choices.journal: I turned {child}’s question about my life into advice.

rows.reason: Give three rehearsal choices distinct spoken and physical endings.

before.title: Is this thing on?
before.body: At assembly rehearsal, {teacher} asks you to test the microphone. You say “Is this thing on?” The empty hall asks it back.

choices.label: Practise the actual announcement
choices.title: Clear enough
choices.result: You slow down and read it through. {teacher} asks you to keep that pace.
choices.journal: I practised reading an announcement into the assembly microphone.

choices.label: Ask how to stop rushing
choices.title: Room for a breath
choices.result: {teacher} marks pauses on the page. The announcement becomes easier to read.
choices.journal: I asked {teacher} for help speaking more slowly.

choices.label: Try an impressive monster noise
choices.title: Sound check complete
choices.result: It is impressive. {teacher} moves the microphone out of reach for the moment.
choices.journal: I tested an assembly microphone with a monster noise.

after.title: Is this thing on?
after.body: At assembly rehearsal, {teacher} asks you to test the microphone. You say “Is this thing on?” The empty hall asks it back.

choices.label: Practise the actual announcement
choices.title: Clear enough
choices.result: You read the announcement slowly. The hall repeats the final word after you. You wait for it to finish before taking a small, unnecessary bow.
choices.journal: I practised reading an announcement into the assembly microphone.

choices.label: Ask how to stop rushing
choices.title: Room for a breath
choices.result: {teacher} marks places to breathe. You get through the sentence without squeaking at the end. The announcement is about lunch, which makes the improvement easier to appreciate.
choices.journal: I asked {teacher} for help speaking more slowly.

choices.label: Try an impressive monster noise
choices.title: Sound check complete
choices.result: Your noise fills the entire hall. {teacher} lowers the volume, then moves the microphone. You try the noise once more without amplification. It loses some authority.
choices.journal: I tested an assembly microphone with a monster noise.
